public_rationale: Sora's documented failures show that its original outputs lacked consistent physical correctness. They do not establish that there was no way to encode and guarantee the named properties. The theoretical papers address narrower formal questions and do not settle Sora's constraint capabilities. The turbulence GAN enforces a specialized conservation constraint, so it does not contradict the contextual claim about general real-world generation. Neither side meets the stated criteria.
limitations: An unsuccessful search for a guarantee does not prove that none was possible.
Published qualitative failures do not establish an architectural impossibility.
The assessment concerns methods available in February 2024, not later model improvements.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Sora, like other generative AI systems, has no way to encode and guarantee constraints such as truthfulness or obeying physics.

statement.excerpt: And like other generative AI systems, there is no way to encode (and guarantee) constraints like “be truthful” or “obey the laws of physics”or “don’t just invent (or eliminate) objects”.

from_speaker: there is no way to encode (and guarantee) constraints
our_interpretation: The ordinary contextual reading concerns the original Sora and comparable general-purpose generative systems, across their intended real-world uses.
The claim concerns enforceable truthfulness, physical consistency, or object continuity, rather than an improvement in average output quality.

A guarantee must cover the relevant property throughout the system's intended domain. Enforcing one conservation equation in a specialized scientific generator does not establish that a Sora-like system obeys real-world physics.
This is a claim about the technical position at the time of the post, not a prediction that no future method could ever succeed.
The target period is February 15–16, 2024, the latest public Sora announcement and demonstration period before the post.
The distinction between lacking an existing guarantee and having no way to implement one is material. Output failures alone establish only the former.
criteria.support_condition: Architectural analysis or sufficiently comprehensive technical evidence establishes that Sora and comparable general-purpose systems then lacked a way to encode and enforce these broad real-world constraints throughout their intended outputs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A method available by the post demonstrably encodes and guarantees at least one of the named broad properties in Sora or a comparable general-purpose system across its intended domain. A narrow formal constraint or improved benchmark score is insufficient.

evidence.locator: Weakness caption beneath the step-printing running prompt
evidence.explanation: The original model's outputs did not consistently obey physical expectations. A failure of that implementation does not establish the absence of any applicable enforcement method.

evidence.publisher: arXiv; Ziwei Xu, Sanjay Jain, and Mohan Kankanhalli
evidence.explanation: The paper argues that LLMs cannot learn every computable ground-truth function without errors. Applying that result to Sora's physical or object-continuity constraints requires an additional argument that this source does not supply.

evidence.publisher: arXiv; Dima Tretiak, Arvind T. Mohan, and Daniel Livescu
evidence.explanation: The method enforces mass conservation in a GAN for incompressible turbulence. That establishes a specialized constraint mechanism, not a guarantee of general real-world physics in a Sora-like generator.

evidence.publisher: arXiv; Adam Tauman Kalai and Santosh S. Vempala
evidence.explanation: The impossibility result concerns particular facts under a calibration condition, while other errors may be mitigated. It neither supplies a general truthfulness guarantee nor establishes that Sora cannot enforce the named constraints.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Technical evidence addressing the original Sora and comparable systems: either an applicable analysis establishing the stated enforcement limitation, or a method available by February 16, 2024 that demonstrably guaranteed a named broad property across the intended domain.
